s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Diffuse poikiloderma on upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
key_facts: Previous treatments tried: systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, IVIG
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles on nailfold examination
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

shortlist.label: Juvenile dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of photosensitive eruption, violaceous erythema, and poikiloderma, along with elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, is consistent with juvenile dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Anti-TIF-1γ antibody-positive dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is a specific marker for this condition, which is a subtype of dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical features such as violaceous erythema, poikiloderma, and nailfold capillary changes are characteristic of dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Although the patient has tried multiple treatments, the presence of photosensitive eruption and systemic manifestations cannot rule out lupus erythematosus entirely

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of clinical features, including photosensitive eruption, myositis, and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, makes mixed connective tissue disease a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, elevated serum IFN-β levels, and clinical features such as violaceous erythema, poikiloderma, and nailfold capillary changes are consistent with dermatomyositis, and the specific autoantibody profile points towards Anti-TIF-1γ antibody-positive dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Juvenile dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the age of onset is consistent with juvenile dermatomyositis, the specific presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is more indicative of Anti-TIF-1γ antibody-positive dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Dermatomyositis is a broader category, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies suggests a more specific subtype, Anti-TIF-1γ antibody-positive dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings, particularly the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies and elevated IFN-β levels, are not typical for lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The specific combination of clinical features and autoantibody profile does not align with mixed connective tissue disease, which typically presents with a combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and polymyositis/dermatomyositis.
